page: Amazon Web Services m7g.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Graviton3 processor family using the arm64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores based on the Neoverse-V1 microarchitecture running at 2.6 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The instance is equipped with 256 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. There is no local NVMe storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in software compilation and memory performance. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, as evidenced by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 253.34 GB/sec for large-block read operations. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the average tier. Additionally, while medium-model LLM text generation is strong, small-model text generation exhibits poor performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based Graviton3 architecture delivers high resource density and strong memory bandwidth per resource unit compared to traditional x86 architectures, making it highly efficient for scaled multi-threaded workloads. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a tradeoff for I/O-heavy tasks. This instance is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation pipelines, database operations, Redis caching layers, and static web serving.
